draft.title: Rural to urban migration in China
card: China has seen one of the largest rural to urban migrations in the world. Hundreds of millions of people have moved from farms in the countryside to cities.
Many went to cities on or near the coast. Factories and service businesses there offered more paid work than farming.
Cities grew very large as workers arrived. They needed more housing, transport and services.
Many workers left their parents and children in home villages. These villages then had a higher share of older people and children.
draft.remember: Chinese workers moved from villages to cities for factory and service jobs, so cities grew and villages changed.

a.q: What mainly drew so many people in China from farms to cities?
opts: Factory and service jobs paid more than farming
Villages had too many older people and children
Coastal cities already had plenty of spare housing
Factories in coastal cities were closing down
a.why: Factory and service jobs in cities offered more paid work than farming, and that drew workers to the cities. The higher share of older people and children in villages is a result of the move, not its cause.
a.clue: Was it a cause of the move, or a result of it?

b.q: Li leaves her village in China for a job in a city. Her parents and young son stay behind. What is a likely effect on her village?
opts: A higher share of older people and children
A higher share of young adult workers
A fall in the number of older people
A rise in the number of factories
b.why: Young adults left for the city, so those who remain are more often older people and children. The share of young workers goes down, not up.
b.clue: Who is left in the village when workers leave?

a.best: Factory and service jobs paid more than farming

b.best: A higher share of older people and children
